scenes.narration: You arrive at the Fair Play Park with your friend Meera. A big kid tells Meera she cannot use the swings because she is 'too small', even though it is her turn. Meera looks at you, unsure what to do.

choices.text: Tell Meera it is her turn and everyone gets a fair chance to play.
choices.feedback: Well done. Rules in the park are the same for everyone — being smaller never means fewer rights. Speaking up kindly for a friend is a strong thing to do.

choices.text: Tell Meera to just walk away — it is not worth the trouble.
choices.feedback: Walking away can feel easier, but Meera's fair turn matters. When something unfair keeps happening, speaking up or asking a trusted adult for help works better than staying silent.

choices.text: Wait and watch what happens next.
choices.feedback: Sometimes watching first is okay, but if unfairness continues, someone needs to speak up or fetch help. Let us see what happens next.

scenes.narration: The big kid keeps blocking the swing. A park helper in a bright vest is standing near the gate. Meera whispers: 'Should we tell someone?'

choices.text: Yes — go together and tell the park helper what happened.
choices.feedback: Exactly right. Helpers exist to keep things safe and fair, and asking them is never 'telling tales'. Going together also makes it easier for Meera.

choices.text: No — helpers only deal with big problems, not swings.
choices.feedback: Helpers are there for problems of every size. Nothing that feels unfair or unsafe is ever too small to ask about. Asking for help early stops bigger problems later.

quizQuestions.question: If a rule at the park applies to everyone, who gets to use the swings when it is their turn?
options: Only kids who ask the big kid first
quizQuestions.explanation: Fair rules apply to every child equally — size, age, or strength never change whose turn it is.

quizQuestions.question: What is a good first step when something unfair keeps happening?
options: Stay silent and hope it stops
Speak up kindly or ask a trusted helper or adult
quizQuestions.explanation: Speaking up calmly or getting a trusted adult involved is the safest and strongest way to handle unfairness.

quizQuestions.question: Is any problem 'too small' to ask a helper or trusted adult about?
options: Yes, helpers are only for emergencies
No — if it feels unfair or unsafe, it is always okay to ask
Only if an adult saw it happen
quizQuestions.explanation: Nothing that feels unfair or unsafe is too small. Asking for help early is always okay.
